Problem It Solves: Organization wants to roll out Microsoft 365 Copilot but does not know whether identity, data access and devices are ready, and fears Copilot will surface overshared content.
Ideal Customer Signals: rolling out Copilot; are we ready; Copilot licenses; pilot licenses; oversharing worries; Copilot surfacing sensitive files; permissions sprawl
Deliverables: Tenant readiness report; identity, data and device assessment findings; oversharing risk heatmap; prioritized Copilot rollout roadmap; executive readout
Phases: Phase 1: Discover tenant configuration; Phase 2: Assess identity, data and devices; Phase 3: Readiness report and roadmap
Prerequisites: Global Reader access to the tenant; named IT and security contacts; list of target Copilot pilot users
Assumptions: Remote delivery; up to 2 workshops; one Microsoft 365 tenant; customer grants access within 5 business days of kickoff
Exclusions: Remediation of findings; Copilot license procurement; custom agent development; end-user training
Microsoft Technologies: Microsoft 365 Copilot; Microsoft Entra ID; Microsoft Purview; SharePoint Advanced Management

Problem It Solves: Sensitive HR, finance and legal content is overshared across SharePoint and Teams, creating risk before and after Copilot rollout; no labeling or DLP in place.
Ideal Customer Signals: Everyone except external users; sensitive HR sites; finance sites; oversharing; sensitivity labels; DLP; data loss; who can see what; access reviews
Deliverables: Data risk assessment (DSPM); sensitivity label taxonomy and policies; DLP policy design and deployment; remediation of priority sites; access review process; admin runbook and handover
Phases: Phase 1: Data risk assessment; Phase 2: Labeling and DLP design; Phase 3: Site remediation and access reviews; Phase 4: Handover
Prerequisites: Microsoft 365 E5 or E5 Compliance (or equivalent) licenses; site owner availability; agreed data classification scheme or willingness to define one
Assumptions: Up to 50 priority sites remediated; up to 5 sensitivity labels and 10 DLP policies; DLP piloted in simulation mode before enforcement
Exclusions: Records management and eDiscovery; third-party DLP tools; on-premises file share remediation; ongoing operations
Microsoft Technologies: Microsoft Purview (DSPM, Information Protection, DLP); SharePoint Advanced Management

Problem It Solves: Agents are being built across the business with no inventory, ownership, permission model or monitoring, creating security and compliance blind spots.
Ideal Customer Signals: agent sprawl; who owns agents; agent permissions; governance for agents; shadow AI; agent inventory; agents accessing sensitive data
Deliverables: Agent inventory and ownership register; agent governance policy and lifecycle; identity and access model for agents; data protection controls for agents; threat monitoring setup; governance playbook
Phases: Phase 1: Discover and inventory agents; Phase 2: Design governance and access model; Phase 3: Configure controls and monitoring; Phase 4: Playbook and handover
Prerequisites: Agent 365 and required Microsoft 365 licensing; admin access to Entra ID, Purview and Defender; named agent owners
Assumptions: Covers agents built in Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 Copilot; up to 25 agents inventoried in detail; remote delivery
Exclusions: Building or fixing individual agents; third-party agent platforms; 24x7 security monitoring
Microsoft Technologies: Agent 365; Microsoft Entra ID; Microsoft Purview; Microsoft Defender

Problem It Solves: Frontline and knowledge workers lose time finding maintenance, quality or service knowledge; the business wants to prove the value of an AI agent with a real pilot group.
Ideal Customer Signals: use case for an agent; build an agent; maintenance knowledge; quality procedures; service knowledge; technicians searching manuals; pilot group; proof of value
Deliverables: Use-case definition and success measures; agent solution design; working agent in Copilot Studio or Azure AI Foundry; knowledge source integration; pilot results report; scale-out recommendations
Phases: Phase 1: Use-case design; Phase 2: Build in Copilot Studio / Azure AI Foundry; Phase 3: Pilot with users; Phase 4: Evaluate and next steps
Prerequisites: Prioritized use case and business owner; access to knowledge sources (documents, SharePoint, line-of-business systems); pilot group of 20 to 50 users; Azure subscription
Assumptions: One agent and one use case; up to 3 knowledge sources; 2-week pilot; time and materials capped at the estimated price
Exclusions: Production rollout; integrations beyond 3 sources; custom model training; ongoing support (see OFF-07)
Microsoft Technologies: Microsoft Copilot Studio; Azure AI Foundry; Azure OpenAI; Azure AI Search

Problem It Solves: Customer must exit a data center (lease ending or VMware renewal) and needs a secure, governed Azure foundation plus a first wave of server migrations.
Ideal Customer Signals: data center exit; lease ending; VMware renewal; VMware costs; servers to migrate; move to Azure; hardware refresh
Deliverables: Azure landing zone deployment; network and identity design; migration assessment and wave plan; Wave 1 migration of up to 50 servers; monitoring and security baseline; operations handover
Phases: Phase 1: Assess and plan; Phase 2: Deploy landing zone; Phase 3: Migrate Wave 1; Phase 4: Stabilize and hand over
Prerequisites: Azure subscription (EA, MCA or CSP); network connectivity plan (VPN or ExpressRoute); server inventory; application owners available for testing
Assumptions: Wave 1 limited to 50 servers; lift-and-shift with Azure Migrate; customer performs application testing; time and materials capped at the estimated price
Exclusions: Application refactoring; database modernization; later migration waves; software licensing costs
Microsoft Technologies: Azure Landing Zones; Azure Migrate; Azure Monitor; Microsoft Defender for Cloud

Problem It Solves: Cloud spend is growing faster than expected with no cost visibility, ownership or commitment strategy.
Ideal Customer Signals: cloud bill too high; no cost visibility; who is spending what; reservations; savings plans; tagging; budget overruns; rightsizing
Deliverables: Cost baseline and savings opportunity report; tagging and cost allocation standard; reservation and savings plan recommendations; rightsizing quick wins implemented; FinOps dashboards; FinOps operating model
Phases: Phase 1: Baseline and visibility; Phase 2: Optimize and quick wins; Phase 3: Governance and FinOps operating model
Prerequisites: Cost Management Reader access to billing scopes; owners for top cost centers; at least 3 months of billing history
Assumptions: Azure spend only; quick wins implemented with customer approval; savings estimates are indicative
Exclusions: Purchasing reservations on the customer's behalf; multi-cloud cost management; application re-architecture
Microsoft Technologies: Microsoft Cost Management; Azure Advisor; FinOps toolkit

Problem It Solves: After go-live nobody owns the day-to-day running, monitoring and improvement of agents and AI solutions.
Ideal Customer Signals: who will run it after go-live; support for agents; ongoing operations; agent monitoring; who fixes it when it breaks; continuous improvement
Deliverables: Monthly health and usage report; agent monitoring and incident response (business hours); knowledge source refresh; minor enhancements backlog; quarterly service review
Phases: Ongoing: Onboard; Monitor and support; Improve; Quarterly service review
Prerequisites: At least one agent or AI solution in production; admin access to environments; named customer service owner
Assumptions: Duration and price are per month (4 weeks = 1 month); business-hours support; minimum 6-month term; up to 80 hours per month
Exclusions: 24x7 support; new agent builds; Microsoft license costs
Microsoft Technologies: Azure Monitor; Copilot Studio analytics; Microsoft Purview audit

Problem It Solves: New AI tools are rolled out but usage stalls because users are not trained, champions are missing and employee bodies (unions, works councils) have concerns.
Ideal Customer Signals: user training; champions; adoption worries; low usage; unions; works council; employee concerns; change management
Deliverables: Adoption strategy and stakeholder map; champions program; role-based training sessions; communications plan and materials; works council and union briefing pack; adoption measurement dashboard
Phases: Phase 1: Assess readiness and stakeholders; Phase 2: Build champions and communications; Phase 3: Train and launch; Phase 4: Measure and sustain
Prerequisites: Executive sponsor; HR and internal communications contacts; access to Copilot usage data
Assumptions: Up to 10 virtual training sessions; materials in English; customer distributes communications
Exclusions: Translation; in-person training travel; technical deployment of Copilot
Microsoft Technologies: Microsoft 365 Copilot; Microsoft Viva; Copilot Analytics
